scope: Research and hardware experiment design; no executable EBR behavior and no completed hardware measurements

hardware_policy.decision: Unresolved behavior and source disagreements are queued for tests on the user's ECP5-85F board; continue collecting other resources meanwhile
hardware_policy.evidence_rule: Retain exact configuration and observation; reproducibility on one device does not establish a universal outcome for vendor-undefined collisions

rules.subject: core_clock_enable
rules.claim: clken gates read and write in the Yosys memory contract

rules.subject: sync_reset_priority
rules.claim: Yosys DP sync reset zero has priority over clock/read enables

rules.subject: sync_reset_write
rules.claim: Yosys uses native synchronous reset only when write and reset are proved mutually exclusive; otherwise it emulates reset in fabric. This does not establish hardware reset-versus-write priority.

rules.subject: async_reset_write
rules.claim: rdarst zero resets the read result; this declaration supplies no general asynchronous write-blocking rule

rules.subject: byte_write
rules.claim: Yosys wrbe_separate writes a group only when CLK_EN, WR_EN and its WR_BE bit are one

rules.subject: read_write_new
rules.claim: Yosys rdwr new means the whole new memory word, including unchanged groups of a masked write; this is not a chip measurement

rules.subject: cross_port_priority
rules.claim: The ECP5 Yosys library declares neither wrprio nor wrtrans; no cross-port priority or read transparency is supplied

rules.subject: initial_read_output
rules.claim: Yosys rdinit zero declares an initial read value; actual configuration/startup behavior still needs a board test

rules.subject: output_clock_enable
rules.claim: Memory guide output-clock-enable selection requires the optional output register

rules.subject: reset_release
rules.claim: Memory guide distinguishes synchronous and asynchronous release of asynchronous reset, but does not specify the internal edge count or its complete enable priority

rules.subject: reset_contents
rules.claim: Reset preserves the memory array; FAQ 3626 additionally describes reset as applying to output registers

rules.subject: raw_cs
rules.claim: CSDECODE from the bitstream already includes the writer's source-level CS inversion; compare reverse3(decoded_word) with raw CS

hardware_cases.subject: PDP36 output half order
hardware_cases.prepare: Use unequal 18-bit halves, including 0x15555/0x2aaaa; hold writes inactive while reading. Preserve the native DOA/DOB routing and INIT manifest.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Read both raw 18-bit output groups at several addresses through each construction path; include a narrow-read reference build.
hardware_cases.observe: Native output halves and logical DO[35:0], before and after public-port interpretation.
hardware_cases.decision: Determine the array-to-native-pin order first, then locate any tool-path permutation; keep INIT and live-write results separate.

hardware_cases.subject: Core CE gating
hardware_cases.prepare: NOREG, matching CS, reset inactive, OCE high; initialize address X to M and seed output from different address Y.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Change address/data at an inactive edge, pulse the active edge with each CE value, then inspect X through the other port at a separate time.
hardware_cases.observe: Port output and stored word X; record disabled-read and disabled-write cases independently.
hardware_cases.decision: Establish which core state holds with CE low, using the other port to distinguish output holding from suppressed writing.

hardware_cases.subject: OCE and pipeline drain
hardware_cases.prepare: Matching CS, reset inactive; place distinct known values in core output and optional output stage using a preceding read sequence.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Apply all CE/OCE combinations for one edge and then several edges, including CE=0/OCE=1 to drain a pending read.
hardware_cases.observe: Output after every edge, with a separate build exposing the NOREG reference.
hardware_cases.decision: Distinguish an independently clock-enabled output stage from CE-qualified OCE; test OCE in NOREG without assuming it is ignored.

hardware_cases.subject: CS comparison and pipeline gating
hardware_cases.prepare: Seed different core/output values and initialize target memory; preserve decoded CSDECODE and raw CS in the build manifest.
hardware_cases.stimulus: For each configured decode sweep all eight raw CS codes; use CE=OCE=1 and include draining an already pending read after CS becomes nonmatching.
hardware_cases.observe: Read capture, pending-stage output and a later noncolliding read of attempted write locations.
hardware_cases.decision: Separate comparator polarity from the effects of CS on core access and the optional output register.

hardware_cases.subject: Synchronous reset priority and writing
hardware_cases.prepare: RESETMODE=SYNC; nonzero memory and output values, both write groups enabled; keep the other port idle at the tested edge.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Assert reset across one active edge for every enable combination, then release and read target memory through the other port at a separate time.
hardware_cases.observe: Output at the reset edge, after release, and array contents after the attempted simultaneous write.
hardware_cases.decision: Measure reset versus CE/OCE/CS and distinguish resetting output from suppressing the write.

hardware_cases.subject: Asynchronous reset assertion and release
hardware_cases.prepare: RESETMODE=ASYNC; seed nonzero outputs and memory, stop both EBR clocks away from an edge; use a separate running observation clock.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Assert and deassert reset without EBR edges, then supply four separately recorded EBR edges; repeat with an attempted write while reset is active.
hardware_cases.observe: Reset response without a clock, output at each release edge and later array contents; capture both write-domain and read-domain behavior in PDP separately.
hardware_cases.decision: Establish release edge count and enable dependence; do not infer hidden synchronizer stages solely from the parameter name.

hardware_cases.subject: DP18 partial-write outputs
hardware_cases.prepare: Use three distinct words: memory M, held output Q and input D; toggle the ninth bit of each group too. Reset inactive, CE/OCE high and matching CS.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Apply each mask during a single WE-high edge; capture immediately after the core cycle and after the output stage, then read the array without a collision.
hardware_cases.observe: Each output bit and stored bit; include BE=00 while WE remains high.
hardware_cases.decision: Distinguish held output, whole DIN, old word and merged word, including behavior of the zero-mask write cycle.

hardware_cases.subject: PDP36 masks and read views
hardware_cases.prepare: Initialize all four nine-bit groups with different values; log native BE-to-ADA routing and keep read/write edges separate.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Attempt one write per mask and CEW value, then read all affected subwords using each width in separate builds.
hardware_cases.observe: Stored groups, ninth bits, address matching and 36-bit output order.
hardware_cases.decision: Verify each native write group, CEW gating and narrow/wide views without imposing a DP-style WEA rule on PDP.

hardware_cases.subject: Cross-port collisions
hardware_cases.prepare: Reinitialize between repetitions, use declared clock constraints and a repeat counter, and first establish baseline results with widely separated edges.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Repeat each access pair with controlled phase steps; capture local clock observations and returned data rather than choosing a port priority.
hardware_cases.observe: Read corruption, written contents, masks and variability across repetitions and phases.
hardware_cases.decision: Document the observed collision region and affected bits under measured conditions; deterministic results do not override vendor-undefined behavior.

hardware_cases.subject: Mixed-width overlap
hardware_cases.prepare: Select addresses from the canonical INIT mapping and mark structurally inapplicable relations; preserve raw address contacts and masks.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Run noncolliding reads/writes first, then overlap experiments using separate builds for every port-width pair.
hardware_cases.observe: All affected canonical INIT bits, including ninth bits invisible through narrow ports.
hardware_cases.decision: Validate view matching separately from collision granularity; equal numerical addresses are not a collision oracle.

hardware_cases.subject: Undocumented narrow READBEFOREWRITE
hardware_cases.prepare: Use explicit primitive/configuration settings and confirm resulting CRAM, to avoid a synthesizer rewriting the requested mode.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Alternate writes and reads at the same address with distinct old, new and held-output values.
hardware_cases.observe: Output and stored data for each mode, including the documented-mode controls.
hardware_cases.decision: Record measured behavior for the actual device and configuration; retain the undocumented status.

hardware_cases.subject: Configuration, INIT and GSR effects
hardware_cases.prepare: Use a free-running observer and a manifest of configuration completion, INIT, GSR and first EBR clock; avoid resetting the observer with the signal being measured.
hardware_cases.stimulus: Capture after configuration before the first EBR edge, then first reads, local reset and a separately controlled GSR pulse.
hardware_cases.observe: Startup output, first-read latency and preservation of initialized/stored memory; do not merge POR, local reset and user GSR into one event.
hardware_cases.decision: Separate initialized array contents from core-latch/output-register state and configuration startup.
